I farm 50 mu, so I do not plan like a very small household plot. I look at cost, but my first worry is keeping yield steady across the whole year. In Quzhou with well water, I can push cabbage three times, but I still have to respect the season. Spring and autumn cabbage usually give me the safer yield, so I will feed those two a bit heavier. Summer cabbage is riskier because of heat, rain, and disease pressure, so I will still plant it, but I will not expect the same output as autumn. I finished middle school, so I do not just copy blindly, but I still start from what farmers around me do and then adjust. On cabbage, I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than let the heads stay small. On 50 mu, if I underfeed, the loss is too big. I will use hybrid seed for all three crops because the stand is more even and it is easier to manage on a bigger area. For the first crop I will plough to turn the soil well. After that, with tight turnover between cabbage crops, I will mostly use rotary tillage to save time and labor.
